en: (Second) Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra:
"Discursive thoughts arise known, they remain known, and they pass away known.
Ānanda, you too should uphold this marvelous and wonderful quality of the Tathāgata. Ānanda, the Tathāgata is thus endowed with such marvelous and wonderful qualities."
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to the Gandhamādana shrine.
“Very well, Venerable Sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One rose from his seat and proceeded toward the Gandhamādana shrine; the venerable Ānanda, placing his sitting mat over his shoulder, followed closely behind the Blessed One.

...continuously following ... out of compliance with my wishes. Then the Blessed One, having entered the Gandhamādana shrine, approached the foot of a certain tree. Having approached, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
"Ānanda, prepare a seat for the Tathāgata at this foot of the tree; my back is weary, so I shall rest it for a while."
"Venerable sir," [Ananda replied]. Having thus assented to the Blessed One, the Venerable Ānanda prepared a seat for the Blessed One at the foot of that tree.

The Blessed One sat down on the very seat that had been prepared, and the Venerable Ānanda also sat down to one side of the Blessed One. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda.

"Ānanda, assemble all the monks who dwell in dependence upon the Gandhamādana shrine in the assembly hall. "Yes, Venerable Sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and he assembled all the monks who dwell in dependence upon the Gandhamādana shrine in the assembly hall. Having assembled them,
Having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, as many bhikṣus as there are dwelling in dependence upon the Gandhamādana Caitya, they have all assembled in the assembly hall. Now, it is for the Blessed One to decide the time."
[The Buddha] thought thus.
Then the Blessed One, having risen from his seat, approached the assembly hall; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Once seated, the Blessed One addressed the monks.

Therefore, monks, those dharmas which I have realized for myself, witnessed, attained, and proclaimed— namely, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power,
the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path— in these you must all remain united and harmonious.
Rejoicing together, without dispute, with one-pointed minds, sharing a single purpose, becoming like milk and water mixed together, and illuminating [the Dharma],
you should dwell in comfort. Therefore, monks, as for those teachings proclaimed by me— namely, the discourses (*sūtra*), the songs (*geya*), the prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*), and the verses (*gāthā*)...

The *nidānas*, *avadānas*, *itivṛttakas*, *jātakas*, *vaipulyas*, *adbhutadharmas*, and *upadeśas*—these teachings should be properly and thoroughly grasped by you; having grasped them, they should be retained; having retained them, they should be weighed; having weighed them, they should be scrutinized;
and having scrutinized them, you should practice accordingly.

For what reason? The parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata will take place before long; after the passing of three months, the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata will occur in the vicinity of Kuśinagarī, in the Śāla grove of the Mallas, between the twin Śāla trees.

Then those monks, having heard these words from the Blessed One, some of them fell to the ground like those who have lost their footing on a precipice, their minds overwhelmed by the thought that it was all too soon.
